Title: A randomized controlled study of paroxetine and cognitive-behavioural therapy for late-life panic disorder
Author: Hendriks G-J et al.
Comment: Cumulative week-26 events were obtained by summing explicitly stated sequential counts: CBT 1 treatment dropout + 1 week-26 follow-up refusal = 2; paroxetine 3 treatment dropouts + 2 week-26 follow-up refusals = 5. Randomized denominators are from Table 1 (CBT n=20; paroxetine n=17). The waiting-list arm was not assessed after week 14 and cannot contribute to the requested 3–6-month post-treatment outcome. No RR or CI was reported in the paper's Results, so these fields are left null.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Individual cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: Late-life panic disorder with or without agoraphobia
Medium: Individual face-to-face CBT versus oral paroxetine with medical consultations
Content length: CBT: 14 weekly 50-minute sessions with optional tapering during the 12-week follow-up; paroxetine maintained through week 26
Topic of Content: Treatment of panic disorder with or without agoraphobia
Participant type: Adults aged over 60 years with panic disorder or panic disorder with agoraphobia
Recruitment source: Patients referred by primary care physicians to a specialized outpatient clinic
Outcome measurement: Premature treatment withdrawal during the 14-week treatment period plus refusal of the week-26 follow-up assessment

Author: Christine Barrowclough, Paul King, Julie Colville, Eve Russell, Alistair Burns, and Nicholas Tarrier
Comment: Dropout event counts were not printed as standalone 6-month values. They were obtained by direct subtraction of explicitly reported 6-month availability from explicitly reported randomized arm totals: CBT 27 − 16 = 11; SC 28 − 23 = 5. No RR or confidence interval was reported by the paper, so ratio fields are left null.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Topic of Content: Cognitive-behavioral treatment of anxiety symptoms and disorders

Author: Chen Hui & Yang Zhihui
Comment: The six-month Results table headings explicitly retain N=32 in CBT-IU and N=31 in control, but the paper does not explicitly state arm-specific dropout event counts. Zero events must not be inferred from unchanged Ns under the verbatim-number rule; therefore event counts and RR are left null. Author: Schuurmans et al.
Comment: The paper does not print cumulative three-month dropout as a single arm-level event count. Report_ID: All-cause study dropout/discontinuation by 6-month assessment: BLP CBT versus usual care
Title: LAY PROVIDERS CAN DELIVER EFFECTIVE COGNITIVE BEHAVIOR THERAPY FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH GENERALIZED ANXIETY DISORDER: A RANDOMIZED TRIAL
Author: Stanley et al.
Comment: The paper reports arm-specific dropout percentages and randomized denominators but does not state arm-specific dropout event counts verbatim in the Results text. Event counts and RR were therefore left null under the anti-hallucination rule. The χ2 statistic is the omnibus three-arm test, not a direct BLP-versus-UC test. Usual care is a shared comparator with the PLP CBT arm and must not be double-counted in pooling.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('CBT delivered by bachelor-level lay providers (BLP)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Study Environment: Primary care clinics at the Michael E. DeBakey Veterans Affairs Medical Center and Baylor College of Medicine
Topic of Content: CBT for late-life generalized anxiety disorder
interaction_type: Provider-delivered individual CBT sessions and follow-up calls
Participant type: Adults age 60 years and older with principal or coprincipal generalized anxiety disorder
Recruitment source: Internal medicine, family practice, and geriatric primary care clinics
Outcome measurement: Study dropouts were those who failed to complete the 6-month assessment
Outcome variable: All-cause study dropout/discontinuation by 6-month assessment: BLP CBT versus usual care

Title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Telephone-Delivered Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy for Late-life Anxiety Disorders
Author: Gretchen A. Brenes et al.
Comment: Cumulative events were calculated only by the synthesis-plan-authorized arithmetic on explicitly reported sequential counts: CBT-T 4 + 2 = 6; information-only 1 + 3 = 4. Randomized denominators of 30 per arm come from Table 1. The paper did not report an RR or confidence interval, so ratio fields are null.
